extraction_method: JSON data artifacts fetched verbatim (no DOM scraping), plus one read of the server-rendered HTML for cross-checks. Opened own chrome-devtools page on https://deepswe.datacurve.ai/ in an isolated browser context named deepswe-rescrape-20260906 (page id 3, stable all run). Every evaluate_script was paired with select_page in the SAME tool-call turn and began with a location.href guard that THROWS on mismatch. Under contention from 8 other agents sharing the browser the guard fired on roughly 20-25 consecutive attempts per script before winning the race; every one of those was a thrown error, never a value written to disk. File size on disk was checked after each save. Used the page's own same-origin fetch() and evaluate_script's filePath option. No Node/curl fallback.

artifacts.role: leaderboard tab 'v1.1' (default). 70 harness+model+reasoning-effort configs, 28 distinct models.
curated 16-config selection used by the /blog/deepswe post. Carries no generated_at stamp.
v1.1-vs-v1 re-grading comparison: 9 shared configs plus a 113-task breakdown. Included in raw.json for completeness; NOT normalized (does not fit the model/benchmark/metric record schema).

Per-task metadata for the 113 DeepSWE v1.1 tasks: id, repository, repository_url, language, base_commit_hash, problem_title, display_description, prompt_characters. No model/score data. Included in raw.json for completeness; NOT normalized. scope = 'Tasks attempted in this benchmark version'.

Same 8-field per-task schema and same 113 task count as v1.1/tasks.json, but the payload is NOT identical and the scope label differs: 'All 113 DeepSWE task definitions' vs v1.1's 'Tasks attempted in this benchmark version'. Included in raw.json for completeness; NOT normalized.

new_fields_vs_20260904.summary: Records went from 18 fields to 33-59 depending on benchmark. Nothing from 2026-09-04 was removed; every previous field is still present under its previous name and with its previous value (verified record-by-record, see verification block).
identity_and_provenance: model_slug (the raw artifact slug, e.g. 'glm-5-3-flash', alongside the existing display 'model')
provider_family (the site's own CSS family token, e.g. 'zhipu', 'moonshot', 'alibaba')
harness (the raw row's harness string, kept beside the existing 'agent')
artifact_url (which of the three leaderboard artifacts the record came from)
generated_at (the artifact stamp, kept explicitly beside 'date')
cost: cost_usd_raw (the artifact's own unadjusted mean_cost_usd / median_cost_usd)
cost_adjusted (boolean: does the site display something other than the raw figure)
cost_per_task_usd (report column; identical to cost_usd, which is already a per-task-attempt mean, named explicitly so the report never has to guess)
cost_basis (the raw row's pricing-note string; present only on gpt-6-astra rows)

corrections_to_20260904: date: on 2026-09-04 only the 10 new gpt-6-astra records carried the then-current v1.1 stamp; the other 130 v1.1 records still carried the stale 2026-09-02T15:18:19Z, which contradicted that file's own meta note claiming all 70 configs had been updated. All 140 v1.1 records here carry the artifact's actual generated_at, 2026-09-03T22:24:37.984682+00:00.
reasoning_effort on curated rows is now taken from the artifact's own 'reasoning_efforts' field rather than left implicit, and 'reasoning_efforts' is also kept verbatim.
date on the 32 curated records is now an explicit null instead of an absent key; that artifact genuinely carries no generated_at.
notes: AGENT/SCAFFOLD: every row on this site was run with the 'mini-swe-agent' harness. Kept as its own 'agent' field, never merged into the model name.

COST ADJUSTMENT, now measured rather than assumed: raw.json holds the untouched artifacts, whose mean_cost_usd is priced at the model's original API rates. The site displays a different figure for 7 models. This run did not take that on faith: the server-rendered HTML of the v1.1 tab embeds the fully-rendered row objects, so the displayed mean_cost_usd was read straight out of it for all 70 v1.1 configs and compared against raw. 19 of 70 v1.1 configs differ, covering exactly the 7 models named in previous runs: glm-5-3-flash (x0.5), gemini-3-6-flash (x0.5), gpt-5-6-luna (x0.2, all 5 efforts), gpt-5-6-terra (x0.8, all 5 efforts), gpt-5-6-sol (x0.76-0.77, all 5 efforts, effort-dependent so not a flat multiplier), deepseek-v4-pro (x6.90) and deepseek-v4-flash (x4.63). Note that the deepseek adjustments are INCREASES, not discounts. All 70 of these displayed values match 2026-09-04's normalized cost_usd to within 1e-9, which independently confirms the earlier run's figures.

COST ADJUSTMENT on the v1 and curated tabs: those tabs are not server-rendered, so their displayed costs could not be observed the same way without clicking through the UI. Their artifacts are byte-for-byte identical to 2026-09-04, so their adjusted cost_usd is carried forward verbatim from that file. Exactly one config is affected in each: mini_swe_agent_deepseek_v4_pro_default, adjusted x0.25 in both. This is a carry-forward, not an observation, and should be re-derived if the v1 artifact ever changes.

PROVIDER: no longer inherited on faith. Re-derived this run from the site's own rendering: the CSS custom property '--family-<x>' on the scatter labels gives a family token for 21 of the 28 v1.1 models, and the /icons/<Vendor>.svg filename on the bar rows gives a vendor for 16. The two agree everywhere they overlap. Families seen: openai, google, anthropic, xai, deepseek, meta, zhipu, alibaba, moonshot. Models covered by neither (older v1-only entries) fall back to the 2026-09-04 mapping. gpt-6-astra additionally carries an explicit 'provider':'openai' in the raw artifact, which matches. Zero records have a null provider.

MODEL NAMES: display names reproduce the site's slug->display transform (join two adjacent tokens with '.' when the second is purely numeric and the first ends in a digit, else with '-'; strip a trailing '-preview'). This run verified the transform against the site's own rendered labels rather than only inferring it: every display name produced matches a key in the rendered family/icon maps.

RANK: recomputed from scratch per (benchmark, metric) by score descending, with ties broken by the artifact's own row order, which is the site's own sort. pass@1 ranks are identical to 2026-09-04 across all three benchmarks. 13 DeepSWE v1.1 pass@4 records changed rank position purely because of tie ordering: 2026-09-04 appended the then-new gpt-6-astra rows after the pre-existing tied rows, whereas this run orders every tie by artifact position. No score changed and no model crossed a distinct score boundary. pass@4 has heavy ties (e.g. six configs share 80.53%), so these positions were always somewhat arbitrary.

METRICS: pass@1 = attempt pass rate over scored rollout attempts. pass@4 = tasks with at least one passing rollout divided by tasks attempted. Context-window failures and agent timeouts are scored failures; provider/verifier/network errors are excluded. Efficiency aggregates are over every scored attempt. Definitions taken verbatim from the artifact's 'unit' field, unchanged.
ci_half_pct / ci_lo_pct / ci_hi_pct are attached to pass@1 records only. The artifact's CI is computed on the attempt pass rate, so attaching it to a pass@4 record would misattribute it.
context_window: OMITTED, as before. median_peak_context_tokens is carried under its own name instead, and is null for gpt-6-astra rows because the source field is null for that model.

MODEL CHECK: 'muse-spark-1.3' is STILL NOT present. Only muse-spark-1.2 and muse-spark-1.1 exist. 'claude-fable-5.1' is also NOT present; the site has claude-fable-5 only. Both verified by scanning the model field of all 230 normalized records.

BROWSER CONTENTION: this scrape ran alongside 8 other agents on one browser instance. Even with select_page and evaluate_script issued in the same turn, the shared 'selected page' pointer was stolen on the large majority of attempts; each script needed roughly 20-25 retries. The throwing href guard is what made this safe, since every lost race surfaced as an error instead of as another site's data being written to raw.json.

changes_vs_20260904.summary: UNCHANGED. The v1.1 generated_at stamp did not move, and all five artifacts fetched on 2026-09-04 are byte-for-byte identical to what they returned today: v1.1/leaderboard-live.json (70 configs, 28 models), v1/leaderboard-live.json (29 configs), v1/leaderboard.json (16 configs), v1.1/v1-delta.json and v1.1/tasks.json. No model was added, removed or re-scored. gpt-6-astra (xhigh) remains #1 on DeepSWE v1.1 pass@1 at 74.12%, ahead of gemini-3.8-flash (high) at 73.83% and claude-opus-5 (max) at 73.65%. The only genuinely new thing on the server side is a sixth artifact, v1/tasks.json, which was never fetched before; it holds the 113 task definitions under a different scope label from v1.1/tasks.json and contains no model or score data. Everything else that differs between this folder and 2026-09-04 is on our side, not the site's: many more fields per record, provider and cost adjustment re-derived from the site's own rendering instead of inherited, a stale date fixed on 130 records, and a tie-break rule change affecting 13 pass@4 rank positions. Any reader comparing the two folders should treat the underlying benchmark data as identical.
